subtopics.title: The Three Ratios and SOH CAH TOA

questions.question: Sine of theta is defined as:
Which side can be identified WITHOUT choosing an angle first?
options: The hypotenuse — it always faces the right angle

questions.question: Scaling every side of a triangle by 10 leaves sine of its angles unchanged because:
options: 7/25 and 70/250 are the same number — similar triangles keep every ratio fixed
The angle grows with the triangle

questions.question: Why must you re-label opposite and adjacent when you switch to the other acute angle?
options: Because the two labels belong to the ANGLE and trade places when the angle changes

subtopics.title: The Special Angles — Values Without a Calculator

questions.question: Halving an equilateral triangle of side 2 gives a height of:
From the half-triangle, tan 60° equals:
sin 45° × cos 45° evaluates exactly to:
The full expression sin 45° cos 45° + tan 60° tan 30° equals:
options: 3/2 — one half plus one, left as an exact fraction

subtopics.title: Finding the Angle — the Inverse Move

questions.question: Hypotenuse 25, opposite 7. The equation for the angle x is:
To recover x from sin x = 7/25, you use:
options: The sine of both sides again
Inverse sine (shift then sin): x = sin⁻¹(7/25) = 16,3°

questions.question: The first sense check on 16,3° is:
options: 16,3 is less than 25, so it fits
16,3 is an even number of minutes
7/25 = 0,28 is under a half, and sin 30° is exactly a half — so the angle must sit below 30°

questions.question: The second check uses the 7-24-25 triangle:
options: The triangle has three acute angles
The other angle is sin⁻¹(24/25) = 73,7°, and 16,3° + 73,7° = 90° — the triangle closes

subtopics.title: Choosing the Right Ratio — and the Complete Method

questions.question: The choosing routine's four steps, in order, are:
options: Mark the angle; label the sides relative to it; circle the two sides that matter; pick the ratio whose letters match
Pick the ratio; mark the angle; label; circle
Circle two sides; pick any ratio; check with Pythagoras; label
Label the sides; mark the angle; compute; verify

questions.question: Given opposite 7 and adjacent 24, the angle comes from:
A calculator returning sin 30° ≠ 0,5 signals:
options: A broken calculator that must be replaced
That 30° is a special angle with no sine
Wrong mode — likely radians; find the D on the display before trusting anything

questions.question: Plain function or inverse — what decides?
options: The direction of the question: ratio or side wanted, plain function; angle wanted, inverse

subtopics.title: Where You Stand Decides the Names

questions.question: On the playground slide, the hypotenuse is:
options: The slide itself — the slant facing the square corner, and its name never changes
Whichever side is longest from where you sit

questions.question: Sitting at the BOTTOM angle, the ladder is the opposite. Climbing to the TOP angle makes the ladder:
options: The adjacent — what faced you now runs beside you

questions.question: The airtime-per-rand picture explains that:
options: Bigger vouchers load more total airtime, so bigger triangles have bigger sines
The RATE stays fixed regardless of size — just as a ratio stays fixed for a given angle in any size triangle

subtopics.title: Two Triangles You Can Rebuild Anywhere

questions.question: The folded square serviette of side 1 delivers:
options: A diagonal of √2 and two 45° corners — so sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2 and tan 45° = 1
A diagonal of 2 and two 60° corners

questions.question: tan 60° × tan 30° equals exactly:
Why must 3/2 NOT be converted to 1,5 in a no-calculator question?
options: Because decimals are always wrong in maths
The question tests EXACT values — the exact fraction is the finished answer, and decimalising discards the tested skill
Because fractions are quicker to write

questions.question: Forward gear and reverse gear stand for:
options: Angle in, ratio out (sine); ratio in, angle out (inverse sine) — one machine, two directions

questions.question: The 25 m slide with its top 7 m up makes an angle with the ground of:
The two-check defence of 16,3° is:
options: It is an acute angle, and acute angles are always right
0,28 is under a half so the angle sits below 30°; and 16,3° + 73,7° = 90° closes the 7-24-25 triangle

questions.question: Old side-labels must be abandoned when a question moves to a new angle because:
options: Opposite and adjacent swap the moment the reference angle changes
